Subject: Re: Capacity ask & timing for Q3 pilot

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. We just pulled the program-level forecast for our Q3 pilot and it's looking like we need to be able to sustain ~120 concurrent seats (90p95 SLOs) for the first 6 weeks, peaking at ~160 during internal load-testing windows. We know you mentioned dedicated capacity as the cleanest option; major questions from procurement and infra are:

- What procurement lead times are realistic if we want on-prem or OEM-provided racks (i.e., SuperGPU SKUs)?
- If that timeline slips, what cloud reserved capacity or backstop options does Redwood recommend to avoid a launch delay?

We'd appreciate a short scenario matrix (best/likely/worst) with dates and action items so our procurement team can plan contracting. We also need a quote they can circulate (line-item: GPUs, rack integration, install, SLA + support).

Can you loop in the appropriate vendor contacts and share proposed fallback plans by next Tue (6/17)?

Thanks,
Maya
Procurement, AcmeAI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask & timing for Q3 pilot

Maya — thanks, this is helpful. I'm attaching a capacity scenario matrix that lays out three paths:

A) Dedicated OEM onramp (SuperGPU racks) — target 10–12 week lead time from PO to usable capacity (best case 8 weeks if stock available), requires deposit and install window.
B) Hybrid: partial OEM + cloud reserved pool — OEM for steady state, cloud reserved short-term to cover the initial 6 weeks. Cloud reservations can be procured in ~3 weeks but at a higher blended unit cost.
C) Cloud-first with reserved & burst — fastest (2–3 week procurement for reserved slots) but higher cost and potential performance variance for cold KV/cache behavior.

I flagged key decision points and vendor contacts in the spreadsheet, plus two contingency escape hatches: 1) short-term marketplace reserved capacity (Jill Park at CloudCo), 2) bridged capacity from our shared staging pool (we can commit a tranche for 4–6 weeks if agreed).

Next actions I propose:
- Acme selects preferred scenario by 6/13 so we can start quotes/POs.
- Redwood to request OEM pricing and install windows from SuperGPU by 6/14.
- If Acme wants hybrid, we will open cloud reserve with CloudCo and share costs by 6/15.

Attaching the scenario matrix + the OEM quote we prelim received last month for reference.

Neha
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Karthik —

We ran the ask against our available inventory and allocation queue. Quick summary:

- Current lead time for the SuperGPU-8xA100 rack (integrated) is ~9–11 weeks from signed PO; we can accelerate to 6–7 weeks if Acme signs a prioritized SLA and agrees to a 30% up-front deposit (this requires a pricing premium).
- If Acme needs delivery within 3–4 weeks, we can only offer cloud-backed bare-metal (partner colo) or Q2 returns — limited availability.

I'll put a redlined quote in this thread with a prioritized SKU bundle and a line for expedited handling. Also note: shipping windows into West Coast datacenters have a 3–5 day variability due to port congestion; if the install window is immovable, consider air freight for critical racks (adds ~7–10% to hardware + logistics).

Victor
Director, OEM Sales — SuperGPU

[Attachment: SuperGPU_quote_v2_redline.pdf (48 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask & timing for Q3 pilot

Quick note — from an operational standpoint, if Acme selects the hybrid path we recommend the following concrete sizing & gating:

- Week 0–6: Reserve 40 reserved cloud slots (r5g-style equivalent) + 80 seats on Redwood shared staging tranche (we can carve out isolated KV-cache lanes).
- Week 7–12: Bring up 2 SuperGPU racks (targeted throughput ~160 seats) and progressively shift traffic by route policy.
- Rollout gating: start canary at 10% traffic, validate latency & cache hit rates, then 25% / 50% / 100% over 5 days.

Ben added: pricing delta for hybrid (cloud premium + redwood staging tranche) vs. OEM only is estimated ~18% higher over the first 8 weeks but reduces risk of launch slip.

Ben
Head of Dedicated Programs, Redwood Inference
